findings.title: Import-time dynamic loading of a script module
findings.message: Executing scripts/release-sdk.py at import time runs arbitrary module-level code as a side effect of importing package-app.py, and fails with an obscure error (None spec/loader) if the file is missing. It also couples the app packager to an SDK release script's internals (git_output, source_state, release_gates).
findings.suggestion: Lazy-load the policy module only when public=True, and check the spec/loader for None; better, move shared policy into an importable module.

findings.title: Release gates invoked in private mode
findings.message: release_gates is now called for every packaging run including private. If it enforces checks even when public is False (or depends on git state), previously working private packaging can fail. The release metadata is also now required to satisfy the policy module's schema.
findings.suggestion: Confirm release_gates is a no-op for public=False, or only call it when public is True; add a test for private mode with a non-git checkout.

findings.title: Authorization recheck occurs before publication, leaving a window
findings.message: The public authorization recheck is placed inside the `if target == "darwin"` block and happens after the output check but the output mkdir follows immediately; the earlier gates were sampled before a long staging/codesign phase. A TOCTOU window remains between the recheck and publishing/moving files (shutil.move into output), so a source change in that window is not detected, and the manifest claims authorization.
findings.suggestion: Perform the final recheck after files are moved and verified, immediately before returning, and remove the output on failure.
